thm-qa-projective-operator-closeness-bou:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space ([[def-inner-product-space]]) with a fixed orthonormal computational basis $B$ ([[def-orthogonal-vectors-sets-and-orthonormal-bases]]), and let $U,V:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H$ be unitary operators, meaning invertible linear isometries ([[def-linear-isometry-and-orthogonal-or-unitary-operator]]). For a unit vector $\psi$, write $U\psi=\sum_{b\in B}\alpha_b|b\rangle$ and $V\psi=\sum_{b\in B}\beta_b|b\rangle$, and define their output laws by $p_U^\psi(b)=|\alpha_b|^2$ and $p_V^\psi(b)=|\beta_b|^2$. Unitarity and orthonormality make these finite probability laws ([[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]). For laws $p,q$ on $B$, define total variation by $d_{\rm TV}(p,q):=\tfrac12\sum_{b\in B}|p(b)-q(b)|$. Define projective operator distance by $d_{\rm pr}(U,V):=\inf_{|\lambda|=1}\|U-\lambda V\|$, where $\|\cdot\|$ is the operator norm. If $d_{\rm pr}(U,V)\le\varepsilon$ for $\varepsilon\ge0$, then

$$d_{\rm TV}(p_U^\psi,p_V^\psi)\le\varepsilon.$$

The same bound therefore holds for every computational-basis output law of the two operators. The proof verifies directly that multiplying a vector by a unit scalar leaves these coordinate probabilities unchanged.
lem-qa-pi-over-two-exceeds-sqrt-two:
## Statement

With $\pi$ defined by the first positive zero of cosine, one has
$$\sqrt2<\frac\pi2.$$
def-qa-cyclic-quantum-fourier-transform:
## Definition

For an integer $N\ge1$, let $\mathcal F_N$ be the negative-sign, $N^{-1/2}$-normalized transform of [[def-unitary-discrete-fourier-transform-on-z-mod-n]]. Define the **cyclic quantum Fourier transform** by $\operatorname{QFT}_N:=\mathcal F_N^{-1}$. The inverse exists by [[thm-finite-fourier-inversion]], and its matrix on the standard basis indexed by $0,\ldots,N-1$ is

$$\operatorname{QFT}_N|x\rangle=N^{-1/2}\sum_{y=0}^{N-1}e^{2\pi ixy/N}|y\rangle,\qquad 0\le x<N.$$

Here the standard-basis ket convention is the one specified by [[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]]. Thus the transform has the positive sign and the same $N^{-1/2}$ normalization as the inverse Fourier formula. At $N=1$ it is the identity on the one-dimensional register. In the binary specialization $N=2^n$, the circuit page writes each index in its unique base-two expansion.
lem-qa-binary-qft-product-factorization:
## Statement

Let $n\ge0$, $N=2^n$, and take the input word $(x_{n-1},\ldots,x_0)$ in wire order $q_{n-1},\ldots,q_0$. By the big-endian index convention, its integer is $x=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}x_i2^i$, with $x_i\in\{0,1\}$. For $0\le j<n$, set

$$R_j:=2^{-1/2}\bigl(|0\rangle+e^{2\pi i\sum_{i=0}^{j}x_i2^{-(j-i+1)}}|1\rangle\bigr).$$

With the register order $q_{n-1},\ldots,q_0$, the standard-basis output $\operatorname{QFT}_{2^n}|x\rangle$ is $R_0\otimes R_1\otimes\cdots\otimes R_{n-1}$. The ordered factors immediately before the final wire-reversal permutation of the exact circuit are $R_{n-1}\otimes\cdots\otimes R_0$. For $n=0$, both are the empty tensor product, interpreted as the scalar $1$.
lem-qa-tensor-extension-preserves-operat:
## Statement

Let $S$ and $R$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces with specified finite orthonormal bases, and let $T:S\to S$ be linear. With the product inner product on $S\otimes R$,

$$\lVert T\otimes I_R\rVert=\lVert T\rVert.$$

If $P$ is a unitary wire permutation on a finite ordered tensor register, then conjugating an endomorphism $A$ by $P$ preserves its operator norm: $\lVert PAP^{-1}\rVert=\lVert A\rVert$. Thus a one- or two-register gate has the same operator norm after identity factors are added on spectators and its wires are moved to their declared positions.
lem-qa-swap-is-three-cnot-circuit:
## Statement

On two ordered qubit wires, let $S$ be the wire-swap permutation $|a,b\rangle\mapsto|b,a\rangle$. Let $C_{12}$ be the CNOT with wire 1 controlling wire 2, so $C_{12}|a,b\rangle=|a,b\oplus a\rangle$, and define the reverse orientation by $C_{21}|a,b\rangle=|a\oplus b,b\rangle$, extending both actions linearly; here $\oplus$ is addition modulo two. The operator identity

$$S=C_{12}C_{21}C_{12}$$

holds, where products act right to left. Therefore the swap of two wires has an exact three-CNOT implementation with no ancillas.
def-qa-qft-gate-cost-model:
## Definition

The **ideal binary-QFT gate-count model** treats each Hadamard $H$ and each exact controlled phase $\mathrm{CP}_s$ as one elementary gate, for integer $s\ge2$, where

$$H=2^{-1/2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad \mathrm{CP}_s=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1,e^{2\pi i/2^s}).$$

A named SWAP, the wire permutation from [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], counts as one two-qubit gate. If the implementation expands each SWAP into three exact CNOT gates of [[def-qc-cnot-and-control-target-order]], count those three CNOTs in place of that SWAP. These conventions refine the one-qubit alphabet, controlled-phase rotation and elementary circuit-resource interfaces of [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]], [[def-qc-controlled-phase-rotation]] and [[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]].

The **finite-set synthesis model** keeps ideal gate count separate from compiled gate count. A one- or two-qubit target block is assigned a projective operator-error tolerance $\delta>0$; a scalar phase returned by the compiler is retained as metadata for the whole standalone circuit. Each CNOT expanded from a SWAP is exact in this model. Any compiled-count theorem must state the fixed-arity decomposition, finite alphabet, inverse-closure, density, exact-arithmetic and compiler-threshold hypotheses it uses. In particular, it makes no claim about classical bit-time for computing an arbitrary target-angle description. This is a cost convention; correctness and compiler resource bounds are separate theorems.
alg-qa-exact-binary-qft-circuit:
## Definition

Input: an $n$-qubit register with ordered wires $q_{n-1},\ldots,q_0$, $n\ge0$. The input integer is encoded by $x=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}x_j2^j$ in the computational basis, as specified by [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]].

Output: the following finite gate list, defining a unitary by the circuit semantics of [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]] on the ordered-register syntax of [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]], and using no ancillas.

1. For $j=n-1,n-2,\ldots,0$, complete the following block before proceeding to the next $j$: apply $H$ to target $q_j$; then, for $i=0,1,\ldots,j-1$ in that order, apply $\mathrm{CP}_{j-i+1}$ to the pair $(q_i,q_j)$, with $q_i$ as control and $q_j$ as target. Here $\mathrm{CP}_s$ is the ideal controlled phase defined in [[def-qa-qft-gate-cost-model]].
2. After completing every block in the descending $j$ loop, for $j=0,1,\ldots,\lfloor n/2\rfloor-1$, swap $q_j$ with $q_{n-1-j}$.

The chronological order is exactly the order listed. If $n=0$, all loops are empty and the output is the empty circuit, i.e. the identity on the one-dimensional register.
thm-qa-exact-binary-qft-circuit-correct:
## Statement

For every $n\ge0$, the exact binary circuit of [[alg-qa-exact-binary-qft-circuit]] implements [[def-qa-cyclic-quantum-fourier-transform]] at $N=2^n$: it maps each computational basis vector $|x\rangle$, $0\le x<2^n$, to

$$2^{-n/2}\sum_{y=0}^{2^n-1}e^{2\pi ixy/2^n}|y\rangle,$$

with the declared output register order. Hence its denotation is $\operatorname{QFT}_{2^n}$ on every state. Reversing the gate list and replacing every gate by its adjoint gives the negative-sign inverse QFT with the same ideal gate count.
thm-qa-exact-binary-qft-gate-count:
## Statement

For $n\ge0$, the exact circuit uses $n$ Hadamards, $n(n-1)/2$ controlled phase rotations, $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ SWAP gates, no ancillas, and

$$n+\frac{n(n-1)}2+\lfloor n/2\rfloor=O(n^2)$$

ideal gates in the model of [[def-qa-qft-gate-cost-model]]. If every SWAP is expanded into three exact CNOTs, the circuit instead has $3\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ CNOTs in place of the SWAPs.
alg-qa-truncated-binary-qft-circuit:
## Definition

Input: an $n$-qubit ordered register as in [[alg-qa-exact-binary-qft-circuit]] and an integer cutoff $m\ge1$.

Output: run the exact binary QFT circuit except omit every controlled phase $\mathrm{CP}_s$ with denominator index $s>m$. Retain every Hadamard and every final reversal SWAP. The resulting gate list is finite and unitary for every $n\ge0,m\ge1$ under [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]]. If $m\ge n$, no controlled phase is omitted and the circuit is exactly the full circuit. The ideal gate-count convention is [[def-qa-qft-gate-cost-model]].
thm-qa-truncated-qft-operator-norm-error:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$, $N=2^n$, and let $m\ge1$ be an integer. For $1\le m<n$,

$$\|\operatorname{QFT}_{2^n}-\operatorname{QFT}^{(m)}_{2^n}\|\le\sum_{s=m+1}^{n}(n-s+1)\frac{2\pi}{2^s}\le2\pi n\,2^{-m}.$$

For $m\ge n$, the truncated circuit is exact and the error is zero. In particular, for $0<\varepsilon<1$, the cutoff $m=\min\{n,\lceil\log_2(2\pi n/\varepsilon)\rceil\}$ gives operator-norm error at most $\varepsilon$.
thm-qa-truncated-qft-gate-count:
## Statement

For $n\ge1$ and integer $m\ge1$, put $\widetilde m=\min\{m,n\}$. The truncated binary QFT uses $n$ Hadamards, $\sum_{s=2}^{\widetilde m}(n-s+1)$ controlled phases, $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ SWAP gates and no ancillas. Its ideal gate count is therefore

$$n+\sum_{s=2}^{\widetilde m}(n-s+1)+\lfloor n/2\rfloor=O(n\widetilde m+n).$$

For fixed $c>0$, if $n\ge2$, $n^{-c}\le\varepsilon<1$, and $m=\min\{n,\lceil\log_2(2\pi n/\varepsilon)\rceil\}$, then $\widetilde m=O_c(\log n)$ and this count is $O_c(n\log n)$ ideal gates. Expanding the reversal replaces each SWAP by three exact CNOTs; no finite-set synthesis count is asserted here.
thm-qa-qft-finite-gate-set-compile-cost:
## Statement

Each retained Hadamard or complete controlled-phase block has an exact no-ancilla decomposition with at most four one-qubit $U(2)$ gates and two CNOTs, uniformly in its angle. Fix an integer $c\ge1$ bounding both counts for the chosen decompositions; $c=4$ always suffices. Assume QC12's fixed inverse-closed dense one-qubit alphabet $G\subset SU(2)$, its exact-real compiler, and a fixed rational $0<\kappa\le\eta_0<64^{-2}$ within the certified compiler range.

Let $n\ge1$, rational $0<\eta<1$, and put

$$m=\min\{n,\lceil\log_2(4\pi n/\eta)\rceil\},\qquad L=n+\sum_{s=2}^{\min(m,n)}(n-s+1),\qquad \delta=\min\{\eta/(2cL),\kappa\}.$$

Compile each truncated-circuit block using that exact decomposition, compile each resulting one-qubit special-unitary factor to operator-norm error at most $\delta$ by QC12, and keep every phase scalar as metadata for the entire standalone circuit. Expand final SWAPs into exact CNOTs. Then the compiled unitary $C$ satisfies

$$d_{\rm pr}(C,\operatorname{QFT}_{2^n})\le\eta,$$

so every unit-input computational-basis output law differs from that of $\operatorname{QFT}_{2^n}$ by total variation at most $\eta$. Its finite-set gate count is

$$O\!\left(nm\,\log^{3.97}(2nm/\eta)\right).$$

This is a gate-count claim under the stated exact-real compiler interface; it gives no classical bit-time bound for generating arbitrary target-angle descriptions and makes no outer-controlled-QFT compilation claim.
